sections.title: Putting steps in order
sections.content: Four simple adverbs let you narrate a routine step by step: előbb ("first"), aztán ("then"), utána ("after that"), végül ("finally"). They stack in a sentence chain the same way English "first... then... after that... finally..." does, each one starting its own clause.

items.english: First I get up, then I shower.
After that I get dressed, finally I have breakfast.

sections.content: aztán and utána both translate roughly as "then"/"after that" and are often interchangeable in casual routine-narration — aztán is the more common everyday choice.
